greeting:
*Cool wind moves through the rough grass around Alaric Red's boots.*

*The last thing that belongs to Earth is still there in memory—an old life, a world without visible mana, Classes, or this impossible second beginning. The present is different: the smell of soil and distant woodsmoke, an unfamiliar sky, and stone walls beyond the public road.*

*Alaric Red is already standing on an uncultivated roadside verge outside the nearby city. Cultivated fields and fenced holdings begin farther away. No one is close enough to have witnessed the instant of arrival.*

*The body is Human, healthy, and eighteen years old. Simple traveler's clothes are already being worn; a small pouch holding five silver rests at the belt. The memories are still from Earth.*

*A translucent interface opens across Alaric Red's vision.*

`SYSTEM INITIALIZATION COMPLETE`
`Origin: Earth`
`World: Avereth`
`Race: Human`
`Age: 18`
`Level: 1 | Rank: F`

`BASE STATS`
`STR 5 | VIT 5 | AGI 5 | INT 5 | PER 5 | WIL 5`

`Location: Public roadside verge outside Alderwatch, Valedorn Crown`
`Arrival Witnesses: NONE`
`Starting Possessions: Simple Traveler's Clothes | Small Pouch | 5 Silver`
`Local Common Language: Integrated`
`Mandatory Quest: NONE`

`CHARACTER CREATION — STEP 1/2`
`Choose your Base Class:`

`Warrior   — Favored Stats: STR / VIT`
`Mage      — Favored Stats: INT / WIL`
`Guardian  — Favored Stats: VIT / WIL`
`Duelist   — Favored Stats: STR / AGI`
`Ranger    — Favored Stats: AGI / PER`

`Your chosen Class immediately applies +1 to both Favored Stats at Level 1.`
`After choosing a Class, select exactly 2 Skills from that Class's Base Skill Pool.`

`Reply with your Class choice.`

*The System waits. Story time does not move during Character Creation.*

turns.input: *I walk towards the Gate of the City Ahead
turns.reply:
The verge ends where the verge always ends: a ditch, a culvert, and then gravel underfoot. The road to Alderwatch carries its morning traffic — a carter walking beside two plow horses, a woman with geese in a wicker crate that clicks and complains at every rut, two boys driving a stubborn calf with sticks. Nobody looks at the blond stranger twice, except maybe at the sword on his hip; a man in heavy armor with a blade is normal enough on this road, and they have their own loads to worry about.

The walls grow as he walks. Grey stone, older than the fields around it, patched in places with paler masonry. The gate ahead stands open — two leaves of banded oak swung wide — with a stone arch over it and a guard post built against the wall's shoulder. Smoke from a brazier drifts sideways in the wind.

A short line waits at the arch: the carter, a tinker with a handcart, a pair of farmhands carrying sacks. Two guards work the gate. One, older, grey at the temples, collects a copper from the carter and waves him through with barely a glance. The other, younger, with a crossbow slung across his back, watches faces. His eyes pass over the geese, the tinker, the sacks — and settle on Alaric as he joins the line, lingering a moment on the sword, then the armor, then moving on. Nothing in it but habit.

The carters' wheels crunch and roll. The line shortens. Ahead, past the arch, the noise of the city comes out to meet the road — hammering somewhere, a dog barking, a vendor's voice rising and falling with the wind.

The grey-templed guard holds up a hand to the tinker, digs under his counter-shelf for something, and says, "Copper each, and state your business, keep it short."

The tinker pays. The line moves again. Two people now stand between Alaric and the guard's outstretched palm.

turns.input: *i pay one copper as i wait for my change and say* My name is Alaric Red and im here to register with the adventurer Guild
turns.reply:
The guard's palm stays out. "No change, friend. Toll's a copper, flat."

He takes it, bites it out of habit more than suspicion, and drops it into his lockbox. Behind him the young one with the crossbow leans a shoulder against the arch and looks Alaric over at the mention of the Guild — the sword, the armor, the clean face of someone who has clearly never carried a Guild plate in his life.

"Guild's down Silver Street," the older guard says, jerking his thumb back through the arch without looking up from his lockbox. "Straight on, second turning left, big hall with the antler over the door. Can't miss it." He waves the next person forward, already done with the exchange. "Mind the step, traffic's thick this morning."

The young guard adds, around a piece of straw in his teeth, "Registering, is it? Bring your copper. Recruit fee's two silvers, and they'll want to know where you're sleeping. Don't tell 'em the ditch." He snorts at his own joke and turns back to watching faces.

Past the arch, the street opens: cobbles worn into shallow ruts, a drain running down the middle, stalls stacked with early vegetables, the smell of bread and horse dung and woodsmoke all together. Straight ahead, the road runs down a gentle slope between leaning timber-framed buildings — Silver Street, if the guard's thumb pointed true — with the second turning on the left already visible, a narrower lane where a painted antler hangs above a wide doorway, travelers and armed figures drifting in and out.

turns.input: *i follow the guards direction and walk to the guild and enter it*
turns.reply:
Silver Street runs downhill under the lean of old buildings, laundry lines strung between upper windows, a farrier's hammer ringing somewhere off to the right. The antler grows as Alaric walks: painted white on a hanging board, iron brackets, the board creaking on its hinges. The doorway beneath it is wide enough for two to enter abreast, and the people drifting through it are a mixed lot — a woman in oiled leather with a longbow slung flat across her back, a fat man in a merchant's coat, two dwarves arguing over a folded paper between them.

Inside, the noise changes. Boots on flagstone, a low hum of talk, a fire cracking in a hearth big enough to roast an ox. The hall is long and high-beamed: notice boards papered over with flimsies along the left wall, wooden tables scattered with dice-players and map-readers, a long counter on the right where three clerks work behind a lattice of iron. Above the hearth hangs a rank-board of carved names and blank plates, and the whole place smells of tallow, ale and wet wool.

Nobody stops Alaric at the door. A few glances find him — the sword, the armor — and slide off. A page boy with a tray of mugs dodges past his hip with a muttered "mind y'self."

At the counter, the nearest clerk, a thin woman with ink-stained fingers and spectacles pushed up into grey hair, is tallying something in a ledger. Beside her, a younger man with a shaved jaw stamps papers in slow, bored rhythm. The queue at the counter is one person deep: the fat merchant, arguing in a low voice about a carriage fee.

The clerk with the spectacles finishes a line, flips the page, and looks up. Her eyes land on Alaric and wait there — not unfriendly, just expecting him to state what he wants like everyone else does.

turns.input: Hello im Alaric Red im 18 and i want to register
turns.reply:
"Straight to it, then." The clerk pulls a fresh form from a drawer, squares it on the counter, and dips her pen. "Alaric Red, eighteen. Spell that surname for me — R-E-D? Fine." The pen scratches. "Trade or Class before this? Any prior Guild membership, any branch, anywhere? And where are you lodged in the city — they'll want a street at least."

Behind the lattice, the young clerk's stamp pauses mid-paper. "Another one," he says to nobody, and resumes stamping.

The fat merchant's argument sputters out; he counts coins onto the counter instead and shuffles off toward the door with his receipt.

The clerk with the spectacles keeps her eyes on Alaric, pen waiting over the next line. "Registration fee is two silver, and that gets you a Novice plate, board access, and the protection contract — meaning the Guild logs your next of kin and takes a cut if you die on contracted work. Grim, but it pays for the burial." She says it the way she has clearly said it a hundred times. "You can answer the questions first and pay after, whichever suits. Do you have trade or Class?"

turns.input: Im a Warrior at F-Rank and i plan to sleep at an Inn for now since im new in this city *i say as i push the 2 silver over the counter to pay*
turns.reply:
"Warrior, F-rank." The pen scratches it in. "No prior membership, then — I'll take the silence as a no." She takes the two silver, checks each against a quick bite, and drops them into a locked drawer with a clatter. "Inn will do for now, but I need a street for the form. Which one?"

She dips the pen again, waits for the answer, writes it, then turns to a cabinet behind her and sorts through a rack of small iron plates. She picks one, breathes on it, polishes it with her sleeve.

"Alaric Red. Novice." She slides it across the counter with two fingers: a palm-sized iron plate, stamped with the Guild's antler on one side and fresh-cut letters on the other. "Keep it on you when you take contracts. Lose it, it's a silver to replace, and you'll queue twice for the privilege."

She pulls a second paper toward her and flips it around to face him, along with a stub of pencil. "Protection contract. Next of kin, or whoever collects if it goes badly. A name is enough — relation optional." The shaved-jaw clerk beside her snorts quietly at his stamps.

The clerk with the spectacles taps the notice boards across the hall with her pen. "Novice board's the lower half, left side. Take a flimsy, bring it here, I log it under your name. Novice work is what it is — rats, deliveries, lost goats. Don't let anyone talk you into splitting a Proven contract on your first week; that trick's older than this building." She straightens the register. "Anything else, or do you want your first look at the board?"

turns.input: *i shake my head and walk to the Quest board to look at the F-Rank Quests*
turns.reply:
The lower half of the left board is the busiest. Flimsies hang three and four deep on iron nails, curling at the corners where hands have brushed past, and a chalk slate above them reads NOVICE in a clerk's square hand. A one-armed man in a Guild sash stands at the upper boards, reading the Veteran listings without hurry.

Alaric's section holds its share of routine standing work:

*Alderwatch Guild standing contracts:*

— **KITCHEN PESTS, REPEAT** — Novice. The Dripping Ladle, Puddler's Lane. Cellar rats grown bold since the frost; traps have failed. Clear the cellar, show the landlord the tally. 12 silver, standing.

— **WOOL CART ESCORT** — Novice. Two carts, Alderwatch to Millbrook Ford, return same day. Roads quiet this season. 20 silver per hand.

— **DELIVERY: SEALED SATCHNEL** — Novice. Guild house to the Salt Gate customshouse, same morning. No peeking; sealed with Guild wax. 5 silver.

— **HERB PROCUREMENT** — Novice. Marsh camphor and goodfellow's leaf, fresh-cut, four bundles minimum. The herbalist's shop on Tanner's Row. 15 silver on delivery.

— **LOST DRAFT HORSE** — Novice. Grey gelding strayed from the plough-field at Barrow's End three days back. Likely west of the city ditch. Finder's fee 18 silver, proof by the brand.

— **WELL REPAIR, ASSIST** — Novice. Rope and bucket rigging, Ashwell court. Laborer's pay, 8 silver a day.

One flimsy near the edge is fresher than the rest, the ink barely dried: **NIGHT WATCH, TANNER'S ROW STOREHOUSE** — Novice. Owner reports someone rifling his stock after dark, twice this fortnight. Sit the night, report or apprehend. 25 silver. Posted this morning.

The paper tacks creak as hands behind Alaric reach past him — the longbow woman from the doorway, plucking the escort listing off its nail. She tucks it into her belt and goes to the counter, not looking at him.

turns.input: *i take the Delivery Sealed Satchnel Quest and go to the front desk to register it and get the sealed item*
turns.reply:
The clerk with the spectacles takes the flimsy, checks the number against her ledger, and writes his name beside it. "Delivery. Good — quick coin, and the customshouse scribes sign fast." She pulls a key from her belt and opens a low cabinet door behind the counter. Inside, a pigeonhole rack; she lifts out a leather satchel the size of a loaf, its flap folded shut under a blob of green Guild wax pressed with the antler stamp.

"Hold it a moment." She takes his hand, turns it palm up, and sets the strap across it. "Feel that? Slightly heavier than the paper inside warrants. There's a Guild charm on the wax. Break the seal anywhere but the customshouse and it reports this house — someone will come looking, and it won't be a friendly chat." She closes the cabinet. "That's the whole job. Salt Gate customshouse, scribe's window on the canal side, ask for Under-clerk Ferren. Get the signature slip back and bring it here. Same morning, so go now — they break for the noon bell and you'd stand about an hour."

She tears a carbon copy of the flimsy and slides it under the counter weight. "Any questions, or off you go?"

Behind Alaric, the longbow woman is still at the counter, haggling over escort pay with the shaved-jaw clerk — "Twenty says per hand, it's written," he says, and she says, "Twenty says per hand with a cart of my own, which I haven't got."

turns.input: *i shake my head and travel towards the Salt Gate customshouse
turns.reply:
Silver Street runs downhill toward the river smell. Alderwatch fills in around Alaric as he walks: a knacker's yard steaming by the lane mouth, two boys hauling buckets of brine, a dyer's cloth hung out above the street dripping pink onto the cobbles. Cart traffic thickens the lower he goes, and the road joins a wider way that runs along the canal — barge poles sliding, ropes creaking, a woman selling boiled snails off a tray she carries on her hip.

The Salt Gate itself is a double-towered arch in the wall, and the customshouse sits beside it, a long stone building with its backside to the canal. Loading doors stand open on that side; carts roll in empty and out heavy. A thin line waits at the public window on the street side — a carter arguing about a tare weight, a fishwife with a crate of eels.

The scribe's window is on the canal side, a narrow hatch with a bench, quieter. A slate above it reads DOCUMENTS & DECLARATIONS. Behind the hatch a young man with ink to his knuckles is copying from a loose pile, tongue between his teeth. A wooden bell-handle sits on the sill with a card wired to it: RING ONCE. WAIT.

Through the hatch, shelves of ledger rolls run back into a dim office. Somewhere deeper in, two voices are going at it over a tariff — "it's hides, always was hides, you don't tax a hide like linen" — "it's dressed hide, Doss, which is practically linen with the hair off."

The noon bell is a while off yet.

turns.reply:
The bell gives a flat clack against the hatch frame. Inside, the copying young man finishes his line, sets down his pen, and comes to the hatch at an amble.

"Documents." He looks at Alaric, then at the satchel strap across his chest. "Ah. Guild run. You'll want Ferren, not me." He turns toward the dim office, calls out — "Ferren! Delivery!" — and raises one ink-stained finger to Alaric. "Moment."

From deeper in, the tariff argument stumbles and dies. A chair scrapes. Heavy footsteps, and a broad man in a quilted doublet fills the doorway behind the hatch — grey stubble, a bunch of keys at his belt, the smell of sealing wax about him. He looks Alaric over once, unhurried.

"Antler wax. Put it on the sill, then step back a pace." He waits until Alaric has done it, then takes the satchel by the strap with both hands, holds it flat, and thumbs the wax. It parts cleanly, no sound, no flash. He reads the single folded sheet inside, face still, then folds it again and tucks it into his doublet. "Right." He pulls a ledger toward him, dips a pen, and writes. Then he tears off a slip and holds it out — then doesn't quite let go. "Name for the ledger?"

turns.input: Alaric Red Sir *i say politely and wait for my receipt for the done delivery*
turns.reply:
"Red." Ferren writes it, blots it with a sand shaker, and this time lets go of the slip. "There. Sign nothing, carry it flat, don't use it for kindling." He closes the register. "Tell them the wax came off clean."

Behind him the young scribe has already gone back to his copying, tongue between his teeth again. Out in the yard a barge horn sounds twice, and the tariff argument resumes at a lower volume — "dressed, Doss, it says dressed on the manifest."

The slip is a strip of stiff paper: DELIVERED — SEALED PACKET, SALTCUSTOMHOUSE, with Ferren's name written out beneath in a heavy hand and the date. The corner carries a small stamp in the same green wax as the satchel had been.

The noon bell is still a while off. The canal-side bench by the hatch sits empty in the sun, and the boiled-snail woman has drifted down along the wall, tray on her hip, calling her wares toward the loading doors.

turns.input: *i make my way back to the guilds front desk and turn in the signature slip and the Quest overall*
turns.reply:
Back up through the gate arch — the queue is thinner now — and up Silver Street, where the dyer's cloth has stopped dripping. The Guild hall smells of lamp oil and old paper as before. The same clerk with the spectacles is at the front desk, sorting brass plates into a felt-lined tray.

She looks up. "Back already. Slip?"

Alaric hands it over with the Quest. She holds the slip to the lamp, tilts it, examines the green stamp, then the signature. "Ferren's hand. Wax off clean, I take it." She opens a ledger, finds the line, writes beside it, and presses her own small stamp into the margin. "Delivery's done. Payment's on your plate when you tap it to the board — four silver, once you're registered." A beat. "Which we haven't finished, mind. Trade and Class, any prior memberships, and where you're lodging. Fee's still two silver. The desk's not going anywhere, but the good board postings go fast after noon."

Behind him the hall keeps up its slow morning noise: a man in mud-caked boots arguing at the postings board, someone grinding a blade on a strap in the corner, a page sweeping grit from under the benches.
